1721528901166375265.a:
It might be useful to coaxial cable devotees to understand how single wire feed works.

The offset feed point sets up a reflectometer increasing the bandwidth by an order of magnitude. That is, a 3 MHz antenna like this is resonant and gainful from 3-30MHz. 50 ohms feed point. t.co

1721529614130893191.a:
You end up with two fields wound around the entire wire reflecting around until everything synchronizes and the signal has a low enough impedance to be radiated.

The differential nature of intertwined state cancels out all local noise sources. This is the reason not to use coax.

1721530230773350769.a: The separation of polarity along the single wire is maintained by the zero crossing point.

1721534920487485645.a: Coax is good for short runs past circuits out to the antenna. It's primary advantage is that it won't shock you or couple magnetically into nearby objects. However it's noisy isn't it? Why? First, it doesn't cancel out local noise. Second, the shield of the coax filters out…
